notes: A core verb for love and strong liking. It is common with people, food, and activities.
ex1_translation: I love my mom, and I love my dad too.
ex2_sentence: 弟弟爱吃米饭，不爱吃肉。
ex2_translation: My younger brother likes rice but doesn't like meat.
ex3_sentence: 我爱北京，也爱那里的人。
ex3_translation: I love Beijing, and I love the people there too.

notes: Usually a noun meaning a hobby or favorite pastime. Keep it concrete and personal.
ex1_sentence: 我的爱好是看书和听歌。
ex1_translation: My hobbies are reading and listening to songs.
ex2_sentence: 姐姐的爱好是打球和跑。
ex2_translation: My older sister's hobbies are playing ball and running.
ex3_sentence: 我的爱好是听歌和看电影。
ex3_translation: My hobby is listening to songs and watching movies.

notes: A basic number word. It often appears with time, counting, and quantities.
ex1_translation: We have eight cups at home.
ex2_translation: Dad gets to school at eight in the morning.
ex3_translation: Our class has eight girl classmates.

notes: A common family word. In speech, people also often say 爸.
ex1_translation: My dad takes me to school in the morning.
ex2_translation: Dad watches TV at home in the evening.
ex3_sentence: 爸爸和我去北京看电影。
ex3_translation: Dad and I are going to Beijing to watch a movie.

notes: A very common particle at the end of a sentence. It can soften a suggestion or request, invite agreement, or add a guessing tone.
ex1_translation: Why don't we go to the shop together?
ex2_translation: It's late, let's go home.
ex3_translation: Let's go sit over there together.

notes: A basic color word. It usually describes clothes, objects, or flowers.
ex1_translation: I have a white cup.
ex2_translation: There are white flowers on the table.
ex3_translation: I bought a white cup.

notes: Usually means the daytime, not the night. It is a common time word.
ex1_translation: I study at school during the day.
ex2_translation: Mom is often at home during the day.
ex3_sentence: 白天我们在图书馆学习。
ex3_translation: We study at the library during the day.

notes: Used in counting, prices, and larger numbers. It often combines with 一 or other number words.
ex1_translation: This bag costs one hundred yuan.
ex2_sentence: 我们学校有一百个学生。
ex2_translation: Our school has one hundred students.
ex3_translation: This bag is one hundred yuan, not expensive.

notes: Most often this means a school class or homeroom. It is very common with numbers.
ex1_translation: Our class has twenty students.
ex2_translation: My older brother is in Class Two, and I'm in Class One.
ex3_translation: Our class doesn't have lessons today.

notes: Usually means half of something. It often appears before a measure word or in 一半.
ex1_translation: I ate half of this bread.
ex2_translation: Mom gave me half a bun.
ex3_translation: I'm halfway through this book.

notes: A common time expression. It is often used with study, work, or waiting.
ex1_translation: I studied Chinese for half a year.
ex2_sentence: 爸爸在北京工作半年了。
ex2_translation: Dad has worked in Beijing for half a year.
ex3_sentence: 姐姐在北京工作半年了。
ex3_translation: My older sister has worked in Beijing for half a year.

notes: It can mean a literal half day or, from context, a long while. Both uses are common.
ex1_translation: Mom was busy at home for half a day.
ex2_sentence: 我找了半天，找到本子了。
ex2_translation: I looked for quite a while before finding the notebook.
ex3_translation: We waited at the mall for half a day.

notes: A common verb for helping someone do something. It is simple and very productive.
ex1_translation: Mom helps me find my schoolbag.
ex2_translation: I help my younger brother carry his schoolbag.
ex3_translation: Please help me open the door.

notes: Often used when asking for help or saying someone is helping. It sounds natural in daily life.
ex1_translation: Please help open the door.
ex2_translation: Dad is helping cook at home.
ex3_translation: He often helps carry things.

notes: This can mean a bag or a package. Context usually makes the meaning clear.
ex1_translation: My bag is on the table.
ex2_translation: Dad brought back a package.
ex3_translation: My bag is in the car.

notes: A very common food word. It usually refers to a steamed bun.
ex1_translation: I ate two buns this morning.
ex2_translation: Mom makes buns at home.
ex3_translation: I want to eat two buns.

notes: Often used as a measure word for drinks. In English, it often translates as cup or glass.
ex1_translation: I want to drink a cup of tea.
ex2_translation: Dad drank two cups of water.
ex3_translation: Please give me a cup of tea.

notes: This is the usual everyday word for a cup. It names the object directly.
ex1_translation: There is a cup on the table.
ex2_translation: Mom bought two white cups.
ex3_translation: This cup is white.

notes: A direction word. It often appears alone on maps and in place words like 北边.
ex1_sentence: 地图上边是北，下边是南。
ex1_translation: On the map, the top is north and the bottom is south.
ex2_translation: North is up, and south is down.
ex3_translation: On a map, north is at the top.

notes: A common place word for the north side of something. It is often used after a location.
ex1_translation: There is a shop on the north side of the school.
ex2_translation: My home is north of the school.
ex3_translation: The hospital is north of the school.

notes: The capital city of China. It often appears with work, school, and travel.
ex1_translation: My dad works in Beijing.
ex2_translation: My older sister will go to Beijing to study next year.
ex3_translation: Next year I want to go to school in Beijing.

notes: Most often this is the measure word for books and notebooks. It also commonly refers to a copy or volume, and it can mean the root or origin of something.
ex1_translation: I have two textbooks.
ex2_translation: My older sister bought three books.
ex3_translation: I bought two Chinese books.

notes: Usually this means a notebook for writing. It is a school-life word.
ex1_translation: My notebook is on the table.
ex2_translation: My younger brother bought a new notebook.
ex3_translation: The teacher's notebook is on the table.

notes: Most often used for comparisons. The basic pattern is A 比 B + adjective or phrase.
ex1_translation: He is a little taller than me.
ex2_translation: Today is a little colder than yesterday.
ex3_translation: Mom gets home earlier than Dad.

notes: Most often this is the negative command word don't. It also commonly means other or separate in words like 别的 and 别人.
ex1_translation: Don't run in the street.
ex2_translation: It's raining, so don't go out.
ex3_translation: Class has started, don't look at your phone anymore.

notes: Use this for a different one or different things. It often comes before a noun, but it can also stand alone.
ex1_translation: I want to read another book.
ex2_translation: This bag is too big; I want another one.
ex3_translation: I don't eat the other dishes.

notes: This means other people, not yourself or your own group. It is common in simple daily advice.
ex1_translation: Don't take other people's things.
ex2_sentence: 别人在上课，我们别说话。
ex2_translation: Other people are in class, so we shouldn't talk.
ex3_translation: Everyone else has gotten on the bus. What about you?

notes: Usually a noun for illness or disease. In daily life, it often appears with doctors, hospitals, and getting better.
ex1_translation: This illness needs to be seen by a doctor.
ex2_translation: Dad's illness got better today.
ex3_sentence: 这个病不大，医生说没事儿。
ex3_translation: This illness isn't serious; the doctor said it's nothing.

notes: A 病人 is a sick person receiving care. It is often used with doctors and hospitals.
ex1_translation: The doctor is seeing patients at the hospital.
ex2_translation: The patient is resting in the room.
ex3_translation: The patient is resting in the hospital.

notes: This usually means not big, and sometimes more generally not very. It is common for size and degree.
ex1_translation: This room isn't big, but it's very clean.
ex2_translation: My schoolbag isn't very big, and it's not heavy either.
ex3_translation: This bag isn't big, and I really like it.

notes: Use this when something is incorrect or not right. It works for answers, writing, and behavior.
ex1_translation: This character is wrong; write it again.
ex2_translation: The teacher said your answer is not right.
ex3_sentence: 这个地方不对，我们回去吧。
ex3_translation: This isn't the right place; let's go back.

notes: This is the usual reply after someone says thanks. It is polite and very common.
ex1_translation: You say thank you, and I say you're welcome.
ex2_sentence: 老师说谢谢，我说不客气。
ex2_translation: The teacher says thank you, and I say don't mention it.
ex3_translation: He said thank you, and I said you're welcome.

notes: Use this to say something is unnecessary. It is common in offers, replies, and plans.
ex1_sentence: 今天不用上课，我们很高兴。
ex1_translation: We don't need to have class today, so we're very happy.
ex2_translation: You don't need to take me home.
ex3_sentence: 不用给我打电话，我在家里。
ex3_translation: No need to call me; I'm at home.

notes: This is the basic negation word in Chinese. It usually comes before a verb or adjective.
ex1_translation: I'm not a student; I'm a teacher.
ex2_translation: Today is neither hot nor cold.
ex3_sentence: 今天我不出去，我在家学习。
ex3_translation: I'm not going out today; I'm studying at home.

notes: 菜 can mean a dish of food or vegetables in general. Both meanings are very common in daily life.
ex1_translation: The dishes Mom made are very tasty.
ex2_translation: In the afternoon, Mom and I are going to buy vegetables.
ex3_sentence: 这个菜很好吃，我还想吃。
ex3_translation: This dish is delicious, and I want more.

notes: A basic food and drink word. It often appears with 喝 and measure words like 杯.
ex1_translation: Dad drank a cup of tea in the morning.
ex2_translation: There are two cups of tea on the table.
ex3_translation: Please give the teacher a cup of hot tea.

notes: It can mean bad or worse, and it is also common in patterns about falling short or differing from something.
ex1_translation: His Chinese is worse than mine.
ex2_translation: It's five minutes to nine now.
ex3_translation: Beijing is still one stop away.

notes: This means often. 常常 is a fuller and even more common form, but 常 is also natural.
ex1_translation: I often go to the shop with my friends.
ex2_translation: Dad often reads at night.
ex3_translation: He often comes to this shop to buy tea.

notes: A very common adverb for repeated actions. It is especially natural in everyday conversation.
ex1_sentence: 姐姐常常在图书馆看书。
ex1_translation: My older sister often reads in the library.
ex2_sentence: 我们常常一起出去玩儿。
ex2_translation: We often go out together to have fun.
ex3_sentence: 我们常常在图书馆见面。
ex3_translation: We often meet at the library.

notes: This is the basic verb for singing. It often appears with 歌 or with a listener.
ex1_translation: My older sister often sings songs for me.
ex2_translation: He sings while he walks.
ex3_translation: My older sister can sing this song.

notes: This is the everyday phrase for singing songs. It is common in hobbies, school, and free time.
ex1_translation: My younger sister likes singing at home.
ex2_translation: Let's sing together this afternoon.
ex3_translation: They are singing in the room.

notes: A basic transport word. In beginner contexts it often means car, but it can also refer more generally to a vehicle.
ex1_translation: Dad's car is on the road.
ex2_translation: I go to school by car, not on foot.
ex3_translation: Dad and I are listening to songs in the car.

notes: Usually this means a ticket for a train or bus. It is a travel word.
ex1_translation: Dad bought the tickets today.
ex2_translation: My ticket is in my schoolbag.
ex3_translation: My ticket is in my bag.

notes: A place phrase meaning in the car, or more generally on a bus or train depending on context.
ex1_translation: Mom's bag is in the car.
ex2_translation: I saw the teacher on the bus.
ex3_translation: My schoolbag is in the car.

notes: A common place word for a station. It often appears with waiting, going, and meeting someone.
ex1_translation: Dad is waiting for me at the station.
ex2_translation: Let's go to the station together this afternoon.
ex3_translation: Let's meet at the station.

notes: A core everyday verb for food and meals. It is one of the most useful beginner verbs.
ex1_translation: I want to eat bread and buns.
ex2_translation: My younger sister doesn't eat this dish.
ex3_translation: I want to eat that bun.

notes: This usually means have a meal, not just eat a specific food. It is very common in daily routines.
ex1_translation: We eat dinner at seven in the evening.
ex2_translation: Dad comes home to eat after work.
ex3_sentence: 下班后我们一起吃饭吧。
ex3_translation: Let's eat together after work.

notes: 出 is a direction word about moving outward. It often appears in forms like 出来 and 出去.
ex1_translation: He came out of the room.
ex2_translation: It's raining, so we're not going out.
ex3_translation: Call me after you go out.

notes: Use this when someone or something moves out toward the speaker. It is a very common direction complement.
ex1_translation: My younger brother came out of the room.
ex2_translation: The teacher asked me to come out for a moment.
ex3_translation: Please come out; we're at the door.

notes: Use this when someone goes out away from where the speaker is. It is common for plans and movement.
ex1_translation: It's raining, and I don't want to go out.
ex2_translation: Let's go out to eat tonight.
ex3_translation: It's raining, so don't go out to play.

notes: A common verb for wearing clothes. It is used with clothing and shoes.
ex1_translation: I'm wearing white clothes to school today.
ex2_translation: My older sister puts on new clothes to go to the shop.
ex3_translation: He is wearing white clothes today.

notes: Usually a noun for a bed. It often appears with sleep and room words.
ex1_translation: My younger brother is asleep in bed.
ex2_translation: My bed isn't big, but it's very clean.
ex3_translation: My younger sister is reading on the bed.

notes: A measure word for how many times something happens. It is common with numbers.
ex1_translation: I have been to Beijing once.
ex2_translation: I have watched this movie twice.
ex3_translation: This is my first time coming to Beijing.

notes: A basic preposition for a starting point in time or place. It is very common in movement patterns and time expressions.
ex1_translation: Dad came back from Beijing.
ex2_translation: We came out from the library.
ex3_translation: I came home from Beijing.

notes: Use this when something is incorrect. It is common with writing, speaking, and answers.
ex1_translation: This character was written wrong.
ex2_translation: I said it wrong. Sorry.
ex3_translation: Your name was written incorrectly.

notes: A broad high-frequency verb. Common senses include hit, play, do, or make in fixed expressions like 打球, 打电话, and 打车.
ex1_translation: The ball hit the door.
ex2_sentence: 弟弟不听话，爸爸不打他。
ex2_translation: When my younger brother doesn't listen, Dad doesn't hit him.
ex3_translation: My older brother often plays ball after work.

notes: A common everyday phrase for taking a taxi. It is often used for quick travel plans.
ex1_translation: We take a taxi home after work.
ex2_sentence: 下雨了，妈妈打车去商店。
ex2_translation: It's raining, so Mom goes to the shop by taxi.
ex3_sentence: 下雨了，我们打车回家吧。
ex3_translation: It's raining, so let's take a taxi home.

notes: This is the usual phrase for calling someone by phone. It is very common in daily life.
ex1_translation: I call my mom in the evening.
ex2_sentence: 爸爸到家后打电话给我。
ex2_translation: Dad calls me after he gets home.
ex3_translation: Call me after you get home.

notes: Use this for opening things like doors, and also for turning on some devices.
ex1_translation: Please open the door so I can go in.
ex2_translation: Dad switches on the TV to watch a movie.
ex3_translation: Please turn on the computer, I want to go online.

notes: A common phrase for playing ball sports. Context usually tells you which sport.
ex1_translation: My older brother often plays ball with his friends.
ex2_sentence: 下午我们去学校打球吧。
ex2_translation: Let's go to school to play ball this afternoon.
ex3_translation: They are playing ball outside this afternoon.

notes: A basic adjective for size. It is also common in comparisons.
ex1_translation: This room is big and very clean.
ex2_translation: Dad's bag is larger than mine.
ex3_translation: This cup is too big.

notes: A place for higher education. It is often used with study and campus life.
ex1_translation: My older sister goes to university in Beijing.
ex2_sentence: 大学里有图书馆和商店。
ex2_translation: There is a library and a shop at the college.
ex3_translation: My older brother goes to university in Beijing.

notes: This means a student at a university. It is a common people word.
ex1_sentence: 我哥哥是大学生，现在在北京。
ex1_translation: My older brother is a university student and is in Beijing now.
ex2_sentence: 大学生常常在图书馆学习。
ex2_translation: College students often study in the library.
ex3_translation: That university student can speak Chinese.

notes: A basic verb for getting to a place. It is very common with time and location words.
ex1_translation: I arrive at school at eight tomorrow.
ex2_translation: Dad reaches home at six in the evening.
ex3_translation: We arrived in Beijing this afternoon.

notes: A verb for receiving or getting something. It is common with results and things received.
ex1_translation: I got a new schoolbag.
ex2_translation: My older sister got one hundred points on the exam.
ex3_translation: My younger sister got a new notebook.

notes: This particle links the word before it to the verb after it. It often works a bit like an English -ly pattern.
ex1_translation: Mom happily went home.
ex2_sentence: 老师认真地教我们汉语。
ex2_translation: The teacher carefully teaches us Chinese.
ex3_translation: I went home happily.

notes: This is one of the most common grammar words in Chinese. It often marks possession or links a descriptive phrase to a noun.
ex1_translation: This is my schoolbag.
ex2_translation: The teacher's book is on the table.
ex3_translation: This is my older sister's cup.

notes: A common verb for waiting. It often appears with people, places, and time.
ex1_translation: I'm waiting for you at the station.
ex2_translation: Mom waits for Dad to come home in the evening.
ex3_translation: I'm waiting for you at the door.

notes: This noun means the ground or floor surface. It is common in place phrases like 地上.
ex1_translation: My schoolbag is on the ground.
ex2_translation: My younger brother is sitting on the floor reading.
ex3_translation: That bag is on the ground.

notes: A noun for a specific place or location. It is common when arranging to meet.
ex1_translation: The class location is at the university.
ex2_sentence: 我们明天见面的地点在哪儿？
ex2_translation: Where is the place for us to meet tomorrow?
ex3_translation: Please tell me that location.

notes: This can mean a place or a space for something. Both uses are very common.
ex1_translation: This is the place where I study.
ex2_translation: There isn't any room left in the schoolbag.
ex3_translation: There are a lot of people in this place.

notes: A place phrase meaning on the ground or floor. It is often used for where things fall or sit.
ex1_translation: The book is on the ground. Did you see it?
ex2_translation: My younger brother is sitting on the ground playing with a ball.
ex3_sentence: 书包在地上，不在桌子上。
ex3_translation: The schoolbag is on the ground, not on the table.

notes: A basic noun for a map. It is useful for travel and finding places.
ex1_translation: My map is in my schoolbag.
ex2_translation: To go to Beijing, you need to look at a map first.
ex3_translation: Is your map in the car?

notes: A common family word for a younger brother. It is only used for males younger than you.
ex1_translation: My younger brother studies at school.
ex2_translation: My little brother plays ball with Dad in the evening.
ex3_translation: My younger brother and I go to school together.

notes: This comes before a number to show order, as in first, second, or third.
ex1_translation: My older sister is in the first room.
ex2_translation: Today we have the second lesson.
ex3_translation: This is my second time coming to Beijing.

notes: For beginners, the clock-time sense is the most important. It can also mean a small point or dot in writing.
ex1_translation: I go to school at eight in the morning.
ex2_translation: The dot in this character is wrong.
ex3_sentence: 现在九点，我们去吃饭吧。
ex3_translation: It's nine o'clock now, so let's go eat.

notes: This means electricity or electric power. Keep it separate from words like 电话 and 电脑.
ex1_translation: There is no electricity at home today.
ex2_sentence: 现在有电了，打开电视吧。
ex2_translation: The electricity is back now, so let's turn on the TV.
ex3_sentence: 家里没有电，晚上不能看电视。
ex3_translation: There is no electricity at home, so we can't watch TV tonight.

notes: This can mean the phone itself or a phone call. Both uses are common and beginner-friendly.
ex1_translation: My phone is on the table.
ex2_translation: Mom calls me in the evening.
ex3_sentence: 我回家后给妈妈打电话。
ex3_translation: I call my mom after I get home.

notes: This is the everyday word for a computer. It is a common home, school, and work noun.
ex1_translation: My computer is in the room.
ex2_translation: My older brother uses the computer at home.
ex3_translation: The teacher turns on the computer to look at the map.

notes: Prefer the everyday sense TV, especially in phrases like 看电视. The physical device is more specifically 电视机.
ex1_translation: Dad often watches TV in the evening.
ex2_translation: I don't want to watch TV; I want to read a book.
ex3_translation: Grandpa often watches TV at night.

notes: This refers to the physical television device. It is more concrete than 电视.
ex1_sentence: 我的电视机在房间里边。
ex1_translation: My TV set is in the room.
ex2_sentence: 爸爸打开电视机看电影。
ex2_translation: Dad turns on the TV set to watch a movie.
ex3_translation: The TV set is in that room.

notes: Movie is the clearest main meaning for beginners. It is common with 看 and 电影院.
ex1_sentence: 我们晚上一起看电影吧。
ex1_translation: Let's watch a movie together tonight.
ex2_translation: Mom also wants to watch this movie.
ex3_sentence: 我们星期天去看电影吧。
ex3_translation: Let's go see a movie on Sunday.

notes: Movie theater is the clearest learner-friendly gloss. It names the place where people go to watch movies.
ex1_sentence: 我们下午一起去电影院。
ex1_translation: Let's go to the movie theater together this afternoon.
ex2_sentence: 那个电影院在商店东边。
ex2_translation: That cinema is east of the shop.
ex3_sentence: 那个电影院在商场里边。
ex3_translation: That movie theater is inside the mall.

notes: This is the basic direction east. It often appears on maps and in location phrases.
ex1_translation: On a map, east is to the right.
ex2_translation: East is on the right, and west is on the left.
ex3_translation: Is east on the right side of the map?

notes: East side is often the most concrete gloss for beginners. It is commonly used after places.
ex1_translation: There is a shop on the east side of the school.
ex2_translation: My home is also east of the university.
ex3_translation: There is a restaurant to the east.

notes: Use the everyday noun meaning thing or stuff. Do not use the literal east-west reading here.
ex1_translation: My things are on the table.
ex2_translation: Mom bought these things.
ex3_translation: Are your things in the car?

notes: This keeps the core beginner sense move. It is often used for people or things changing position.
ex1_translation: Don't move, I'll show you.
ex2_translation: The wind is strong, and the door moved.
ex3_translation: Class has started, don't move.

notes: Action is the strongest primary meaning for learners. It can also mean a physical movement.
ex1_translation: His movements are very fast.
ex2_translation: I can't do this movement.
ex3_translation: The teacher's movements are very quick.

notes: All is the main meaning. It also naturally means both when exactly two people or things are involved.
ex1_translation: Today we are all at home.
ex2_translation: Both Mom and Dad love me.
ex3_translation: They are all in the library.

notes: Keep this as the verb read. Do not drift into the broader study sense here.
ex1_translation: My older sister is reading the text now.
ex2_translation: I often read this book.
ex3_translation: The teacher reads this character, and I write it.

notes: The study sense is especially important for beginners. It can also mean reading books in a literal way.
ex1_translation: My older sister is studying at university now.
ex2_translation: Dad often reads books in the evening.
ex3_translation: He is studying at university this year.

notes: It is common both as an adjective meaning correct or right and as a preposition meaning to or toward.
ex1_translation: You wrote your name correctly.
ex2_translation: This character is right, but that one is wrong.
ex3_translation: Your answer is correct.

notes: Sorry is the main everyday meaning. It also works as excuse me in polite questions or interruptions.
ex1_translation: Sorry, I came late.
ex2_sentence: 对不起，请问饭店在哪儿？
ex2_translation: Excuse me, where is the restaurant?
ex3_translation: Sorry, I came late today.

notes: Many and much are the clearest beginner meanings. More is also common when it is clearly natural in context.
ex1_translation: There are many people here.
ex2_translation: I want a little more water.
ex3_translation: There are many people in the mall.

notes: Use how many for countable things and how much for amounts or money. Both are very common.
ex1_translation: How many students are in your class?
ex2_translation: How much does this bun cost?
ex3_translation: How much is this bag?

notes: This is the adjective hungry. It is common with time words and food words.
ex1_translation: I'm hungry now and want to eat.
ex2_translation: My younger brother is very hungry after class.
ex3_translation: I'm very hungry now and want to eat.

notes: A family word meaning son. It refers to a male child in relation to parents.
ex1_translation: His son goes to middle school.
ex2_translation: The father and son play ball together.
ex3_translation: His son goes to school.

notes: This is the number two. It often appears in dates, floors, and math-like counting contexts.
ex1_translation: Today is February second.
ex2_translation: There is a restaurant on the second floor.
ex3_translation: Today is Tuesday.

notes: For beginners, meal or food is usually the best gloss. The cooked-rice sense exists but is narrower.
ex1_translation: The meal Mom made is very tasty.
ex2_translation: At noon, we eat a meal with Dad.
ex3_translation: Today's meal is very tasty.

notes: For this HSK 1 run, treat 饭店 as restaurant. It is a common place word for eating out.
ex1_translation: The food at this restaurant is very tasty.
ex2_translation: We're going to a restaurant for dinner tonight.
ex3_translation: There is a restaurant east of my home.

notes: A common noun for a room in a home or building.
ex1_translation: My room is small and very clean.
ex2_translation: My older sister is reading in the room.
ex3_translation: There are many books in my room.

notes: The everyday word for a house.
ex1_translation: This house isn't big, but it looks nice.
ex2_sentence: 爷爷奶奶住在那个房子里。
ex2_translation: Grandpa and Grandma live in that house.
ex3_translation: That house is behind the school.

notes: Use this for putting or placing something somewhere.
ex1_translation: The schoolbag was put on the table.
ex2_translation: The book was placed in the room.
ex3_translation: Let's put the schoolbag by the door.

notes: This means being on holiday or on vacation from school or work.
ex1_translation: School will have a holiday for one day tomorrow.
ex2_translation: We'll go back to Beijing after vacation starts.
ex3_translation: We're on vacation, so let's go to Beijing.

notes: Use this when school has finished for the day.
ex1_translation: After school is over, I go home to eat.
ex2_sentence: 弟弟放学了，在家看电视。
ex2_translation: My younger brother got out of school and is watching TV at home.
ex3_translation: My younger brother went home after school.

notes: The basic verb for flying or moving through the air.
ex1_translation: The plane flew to Beijing.
ex2_translation: That ball flew out.
ex3_translation: That ball flew up into the sky.

notes: Airplane is the clearest beginner gloss.
ex1_translation: I'm taking a plane home tomorrow.
ex2_sentence: 爸爸在机场看见飞机了。
ex2_translation: Dad saw a plane at the airport.
ex3_translation: The airplane arrives in Beijing this morning.

notes: A strong adverb meaning very.
ex1_translation: This dish is very tasty.
ex2_translation: I'm extremely happy today.
ex3_translation: I like this movie very much.

notes: Most often this means minute in time. It can also mean a point on a score.
ex1_translation: It's 8:10 now.
ex2_translation: My older sister got ninety points on the exam.
ex3_translation: It is 9:05 now.

notes: A common noun for wind.
ex1_translation: The wind is strong today, and it's cold.
ex2_translation: It's windy outside, so don't go out.
ex3_translation: The wind is strong today, so don't go out.

notes: This entry is the adjective meaning dry.
ex1_translation: My clothes are dry now.
ex2_translation: The ground is very dry and clean today.
ex3_translation: This cup is dry and very clean.

notes: A common adjective for something clean.
ex1_translation: This room is very clean.
ex2_translation: My hands are very clean.
ex3_translation: Your room is very clean.

notes: This entry is the verb meaning do.
ex1_translation: I want to do this work today.
ex2_sentence: 爸爸在北京干这个工作。
ex2_translation: Dad does this job in Beijing.
ex3_translation: I want to do this job.

notes: A common everyday question about what someone is doing.
ex1_translation: What are you doing at home now?
ex2_sentence: 姐姐今天晚上想干什么？
ex2_translation: What does my older sister want to do tonight?
ex3_translation: What are you doing at home this afternoon?

notes: Use tall for people and high for height or position.
ex1_translation: My older brother is much taller than me.
ex2_translation: This mountain is very high.
ex3_translation: My older brother is a little taller than me.

notes: A common adjective for feeling happy.
ex1_translation: I'm really happy today.
ex2_translation: Mom is glad to see me.
ex3_translation: I'm very happy to see you.

notes: Use this when telling someone information.
ex1_translation: Mom told me that tomorrow is a holiday.
ex2_translation: Please tell me the location.
ex3_translation: Please tell me your name.

notes: The everyday family word for an older brother.
ex1_translation: My older brother studies at university.
ex2_translation: My older brother plays ball with me in the evening.
ex3_translation: My older brother went to play ball with a friend.

notes: A noun for a song.
ex1_translation: This is a song I like.
ex2_translation: The song Mom sings is very pleasant to hear.
ex3_translation: This song sounds great, and I like it.

notes: This is the common general classifier used with many nouns.
ex1_translation: I have a younger brother.
ex2_translation: There are two cups on the table.
ex3_sentence: 我有一个哥哥，一个姐姐。
ex3_translation: I have one older brother and one older sister.

notes: The core meaning is give. It is also very common in simple grammar patterns meaning to or for.
ex1_translation: Mom buys bread for me.
ex2_translation: I call my older sister.
ex3_translation: Please give me a cup of water.

notes: Most often this means with in beginner material. It also commonly means to follow someone or something.
ex1_translation: I go to the shop with Mom.
ex2_translation: My older sister watches a movie with me.
ex3_translation: I'm going home with my older brother.

notes: A noun for a worker.
ex1_translation: My dad is also a worker.
ex2_translation: That worker is working.
ex3_translation: That worker is working outside.

notes: This can mean work as an activity or a job as a noun.
ex1_translation: Dad is working in Beijing now.
ex2_translation: My older brother found a job today.
ex3_translation: My older sister works at a hospital.

notes: Use this for closing things like doors, and for turning off devices.
ex1_translation: Please close the door; I want to sleep.
ex2_translation: Dad turned off the TV in the evening.
ex3_translation: Please turn off the TV, and let's go to sleep.

notes: A common verb for closing or shutting something.
ex1_translation: Please close the door. I want to sleep.
ex2_translation: Dad shut the door after coming home.
ex3_translation: Please close the door, let's start class.

notes: For HSK 1, this means expensive, especially for prices.
ex1_translation: This schoolbag is very expensive.
ex2_translation: That restaurant isn't costly.
ex3_translation: This bag is too expensive.

notes: This means country and often appears in common words like 中国, 国家, and 国外.
ex1_translation: China is my country.
ex2_translation: My older sister wants to go abroad to study.
ex3_translation: China is a big country.

notes: A common noun for a country as a nation.
ex1_translation: China is a country.
ex2_translation: I love this nation.
ex3_translation: There are many people in this country.

notes: Use this for being in or going to another country.
ex1_translation: My older sister is studying Chinese abroad.
ex2_translation: Dad is going overseas to work next year.
ex3_translation: My older brother works abroad.

notes: Keep the basic motion sense of passing or going past.
ex1_translation: I cross the road to go to school.
ex2_translation: Dad drives past this intersection.
ex3_translation: We walked past that shop.

notes: A very common adverb. It often means still, also, or yet, depending on the sentence.
ex1_translation: My older sister is still reading in the room.
ex2_translation: I like drinking tea, and I also like drinking milk.
ex3_translation: He is still in the hospital.

notes: Very common in questions with two choices, where it means or. It can also mean still in other contexts.
ex1_translation: It is still very cold now.
ex2_translation: Do you drink tea or water?
ex3_translation: Will you have tea or water?

notes: Use this for also having something or for there also being something.
ex1_translation: There is also a book on the table.
ex2_sentence: 我有一个姐姐，还有一个弟弟。
ex2_translation: I have an older sister and also a younger brother.
ex3_translation: There is also a book in the schoolbag.

notes: A common learner-friendly word for a child.
ex1_translation: That child is running on the road.
ex2_translation: This kid really likes flowers.
ex3_translation: This child can write Chinese characters.

notes: Treat this as the Chinese language.
ex1_translation: I study Chinese at school.
ex2_translation: Mom can speak a little Chinese.
ex3_translation: I study Chinese at university.

notes: A noun for a written Chinese character.
ex1_translation: This Chinese character is difficult.
ex2_translation: I can write this Chinese character.
ex3_translation: I can't write this Chinese character.

notes: A very common word meaning good. It also often means well or nice depending on context.
ex1_translation: The weather is good today.
ex2_translation: The teacher is very good, and we all like them.
ex3_translation: This teacher is very nice.

notes: Use this for food that tastes good.
ex1_translation: This bun is delicious.
ex2_translation: The food Mom made is really tasty.
ex3_translation: Rice is also delicious.

notes: Use this for people or things that look nice, and for books or movies that are good to watch.
ex1_translation: My older sister looks good today.
ex2_translation: This movie is really nice to watch.
ex3_translation: This bag looks nice.

notes: Use this for songs, sounds, or names that sound nice.
ex1_translation: The song my older sister sings is pleasant to hear.
ex2_translation: This name sounds nice.
ex3_translation: This song sounds nice.

notes: Fun is the clearest beginner meaning.
ex1_translation: Playing ball is fun.
ex2_translation: Beijing is really interesting and fun.
ex3_sentence: 北京很好玩儿，我们再去。
ex3_translation: Beijing is fun, so let's go again.

notes: Use it for numbers like room numbers and for calendar dates.
ex1_translation: Today is the second.
ex2_translation: I'm in room number eight.
ex3_translation: Today is the fifth.

notes: A common verb for drinking liquids.
ex1_translation: I drink a glass of milk in the morning.
ex2_translation: Dad drinks a cup of tea in the evening.
ex3_translation: I want to drink hot water.

notes: Most often this is the conjunction and. It can also mean with in some common patterns.
ex1_translation: Mom and Dad are both at home.
ex2_translation: I want to buy bread and milk.
ex3_translation: Dad and Mom are at home.

notes: A common adverb meaning very.
ex1_translation: I'm very happy today.
ex2_translation: My room is very clean.
ex3_translation: I'm very happy today and want to sing.

notes: It can mean behind or back in place phrases, and after in time phrases.
ex1_translation: Dad goes home to eat after work.
ex2_translation: We go to the library after class.
ex3_translation: After class I go to the library.

notes: A place word meaning behind something or someone.
ex1_translation: There is a shop behind the school.
ex2_translation: I sit in back of Dad.
ex3_translation: The restaurant is behind the shop.

notes: A time phrase for two days from today.
ex1_translation: We have an exam the day after tomorrow.
ex2_translation: Mom goes back to Beijing the day after tomorrow.
ex3_translation: We are going to see a movie the day after tomorrow.

notes: Most often this is the noun flower. It also commonly means to spend money or time.
ex1_translation: There are many flowers on the table.
ex2_translation: Mom bought flowers today.
ex3_translation: This flower is very pretty.

notes: A common noun for words or what someone says.
ex1_translation: I remembered what the teacher said.
ex2_translation: I remembered all these words.
ex3_translation: I have something I want to tell you.

notes: Bad is the main meaning. It also commonly describes things that do not work.
ex1_sentence: 这个地方不坏，很好玩儿。
ex1_translation: This place isn't bad; it's fun.
ex2_sentence: 我的手机坏了，不能用了。
ex2_translation: My phone is broken and can't be used anymore.
ex3_translation: My computer is broken; it has no power.

notes: This pronunciation means to return something or give it back.
ex1_translation: I'll return this book to you tomorrow.
ex2_translation: My older sister gave the phone back to Mom.
ex3_translation: I'll give this book back to you tomorrow.

notes: Use this for going back or returning somewhere.
ex1_translation: Dad goes back to Beijing to work in the afternoon.
ex2_translation: We return to school for class tomorrow.
ex3_translation: This afternoon I'm going back to school.

notes: A common verb for answering a question or replying to someone.
ex1_translation: The teacher asked me, and I answered.
ex2_translation: He didn't reply to what I said.
ex3_translation: You ask me, and I will answer.

notes: Use this for returning to a place.
ex1_translation: Dad returned home in the evening.
ex2_sentence: 我们后天回到学校上课。
ex2_translation: We'll go back to school for class the day after tomorrow.
ex3_translation: This afternoon I returned home.

notes: A very common daily phrase meaning to go home.
ex1_translation: Mom goes home to cook after work.
ex2_translation: Let's go home together tonight.
ex3_translation: We go home together after class.

notes: Use this when someone comes back toward the speaker.
ex1_sentence: 爸爸明天晚上回来吃饭。
ex1_translation: Dad will come back tomorrow evening to eat.
ex2_translation: My older sister will return from Beijing the day after tomorrow.
ex3_translation: My older brother will come back this afternoon.

notes: Use this for going back away from where the speaker is.
ex1_translation: It's too late, let's go back.
ex2_translation: After class, I'll go back to see Mom.
ex3_translation: I will go back to see Dad in the evening.

notes: Most often this expresses ability or knowing how to do something. It is also a common noun meaning a meeting.
ex1_translation: I can speak a little Chinese.
ex2_translation: My older sister knows how to drive and also play ball.
ex3_translation: I can drive, and I can use the internet too.

notes: The everyday word for a train.
ex1_translation: Dad is taking the train home today.
ex2_translation: We're waiting for the train at the station.
ex3_translation: Dad is taking the train to Beijing.

notes: A noun for an airport.
ex1_translation: Dad is waiting for us at the airport.
ex2_translation: I'm going to the airport tomorrow to take a plane.
ex3_translation: Let's meet at the airport.

notes: A ticket for flying on a plane.
ex1_translation: My older sister bought tomorrow's plane ticket.
ex2_translation: My air ticket is in my schoolbag.
ex3_translation: The plane ticket is in my schoolbag.

notes: The common noun for an egg.
ex1_translation: I ate an egg this morning.
ex2_translation: Mom bought a lot of eggs.
ex3_translation: I ate two eggs this morning.

notes: Most often this asks how many. It can also mean several in statements.
ex1_translation: How many people are there in your family?
ex2_translation: There are several books on the table.
ex3_translation: How many people are in your family?

notes: It commonly means remember, and it can also mean to write something down or record it.
ex1_translation: I'm slow to remember this Chinese character.
ex2_translation: Did you remember what the teacher said?
ex3_translation: Please remember this location.

notes: This can mean remembering something or remembering to do something.
ex1_translation: I remember his name.
ex2_translation: Do you remember to close the door when you go home?
ex3_sentence: 回家后记得给我打电话。
ex3_translation: Remember to call me after you get home.

notes: A resultative form meaning to keep something in memory.
ex1_translation: Please remember my name.
ex2_translation: Keep the teacher's words in mind.
ex3_translation: You need to remember this place.

notes: Home is the strongest beginner meaning. It can also extend to family.
ex1_translation: My home is behind the school.
ex2_translation: He misses his family while abroad.
ex3_translation: I'm home, don't wait for me.

notes: A location phrase meaning at home or in the house.
ex1_translation: Mom is cooking at home today.
ex2_sentence: 我们家里还有很多水果。
ex2_translation: We still have a lot of fruit in the house.
ex3_translation: My older sister is resting at home today.

notes: A noun for your family or the people in it.
ex1_translation: My family is all in Beijing.
ex2_translation: It's very nice when the family eats together.
ex3_translation: All my family members love me very much.

notes: Here it is mainly the classifier used for rooms or spaces.
ex1_translation: My home has three rooms.
ex2_translation: There are two rooms in my home.
ex3_translation: The school has three rooms.

notes: It commonly means see, and it also often means meet when seeing a person.
ex1_translation: I saw the teacher at school.
ex2_sentence: 姐姐明天去北京见朋友。
ex2_translation: My older sister is going to Beijing to see a friend tomorrow.
ex3_translation: I saw the teacher at the door.

notes: A common verb for meeting someone in person.
ex1_translation: We'll meet at school tomorrow.
ex2_translation: I want to see you in person.
ex3_translation: We'll meet at the airport tomorrow.

notes: The basic verb meaning to teach.
ex1_sentence: 老师在学校教我们汉语。
ex1_translation: The teacher teaches us Chinese at school.
ex2_translation: Mom teaches my younger sister to write characters.
ex3_translation: Today the teacher is teaching us Chinese characters.

notes: For beginners, the naming sense is the most important.
ex1_translation: This country is called China, right?
ex2_translation: Mom calls me to come home and eat.
ex3_translation: Dad calls my name.

notes: This is the school building where classes are held.
ex1_translation: The classroom building is inside the school grounds.
ex2_sentence: 我们今天在教学楼上课。
ex2_translation: We have class in the classroom building today.
ex3_sentence: 教学楼在学校东边，很大。
ex3_translation: The classroom building is on the east side of the school, and it's very big.

notes: The everyday family word for an older sister.
ex1_translation: My older sister studies at university.
ex2_translation: My older sister watches a movie with me at night.
ex3_translation: My older sister is driving to work today.

notes: Use this for introducing people or giving simple information.
ex1_translation: Let me introduce my family.
ex2_translation: The teacher introduces the school to us.
ex3_translation: The teacher introduces that new classmate.

notes: A common time phrase for the current year.
ex1_translation: I go to middle school this year.
ex2_translation: My older sister is twenty this year.
ex3_translation: I'm studying in Beijing this year.

notes: The basic time word for the present day.
ex1_translation: I'm not going to school today.
ex2_translation: Dad gets off work early today.
ex3_translation: We don't have class this afternoon.

notes: Use this for moving into a place.
ex1_translation: I'll go into the room first.
ex2_translation: My younger brother wants to go inside the school.
ex3_translation: Please go into this room.

notes: A directional phrase for coming in toward the speaker.
ex1_translation: Please come in; it's cold outside.
ex2_translation: Mom came in through the doorway.
ex3_translation: Please come in, it's too cold outside.

notes: A directional phrase for going in away from the speaker.
ex1_translation: I want to go in and take a look.
ex2_translation: The teacher tells us to go in for class.
ex3_translation: Let's have them walk in together.

notes: The number nine.
ex1_translation: It's nine o'clock now, class is starting soon.
ex2_translation: Dad comes home at nine in the evening.
ex3_translation: It's nine o'clock now, have you gotten up yet?

primary_gloss: then; right away; as soon as
notes: A very common grammar word. It often means then or right away, and in some sentences it adds a stronger sense like only then.
ex1_translation: After class, I then go home.
ex2_sentence: 我到家就给妈妈打电话。
ex2_translation: As soon as I get home, I call Mom.
ex3_translation: If you go, then I will go.

notes: A common verb for opinions and feelings.
ex1_translation: I think this dish is very tasty.
ex2_translation: Mom feels that it's very cold today.
ex3_sentence: 我觉得这个电影很好看。
ex3_translation: I think this movie is really good.

notes: Common senses include open, turn on, start, drive, and hold, as in 开门, 开电视, 开车, and 开会.
ex1_translation: Please open the door, I'm back.
ex2_translation: Dad turns on the TV to watch a movie.
ex3_translation: Please open the door, I'm outside.

notes: The common verb for driving a car.
ex1_translation: Dad can drive to work.
ex2_translation: My older sister can't drive yet.
ex3_translation: Dad can drive to the airport.

notes: A fixed phrase for attending or holding a meeting.
ex1_translation: Dad is in a meeting this afternoon.
ex2_translation: We'll have a meeting at school tomorrow.
ex3_translation: The teacher is having a meeting at school this morning.

notes: Use this for joking in everyday conversation.
ex1_translation: Are you really kidding?
ex2_translation: My older sister often jokes with me.
ex3_translation: You're kidding, right?

notes: This verb is used for looking, watching, and reading.
ex1_translation: Look at this character. Is it right?
ex2_translation: Mom watches movies in the evening.
ex3_translation: I'm looking at the map in the car.

notes: A fixed phrase meaning to see a doctor for an illness.
ex1_translation: Mom is going to the hospital to see a doctor today.
ex2_translation: My younger brother is sick and needs to see a doctor.
ex3_translation: Dad is going to the hospital to see a doctor this afternoon.

notes: A resultative form meaning to manage to see something.
ex1_translation: I saw the teacher on the road.
ex2_translation: Dad caught sight of me after coming home.
ex3_translation: I saw the teacher come in.

notes: A common resultative form for seeing something.
ex1_translation: I didn't see your schoolbag.
ex2_sentence: 姐姐在车上看见妈妈了。
ex2_translation: My older sister caught sight of Mom in the car.
ex3_translation: I saw you at the door.

notes: A verb for testing or examining someone.
ex1_translation: The teacher will test us on Chinese tomorrow.
ex2_translation: The teacher isn't examining us today.
ex3_translation: The teacher is testing us on Chinese characters today.

notes: A common noun for a school exam or test.
ex1_translation: I have a Chinese exam tomorrow.
ex2_translation: I'll go home right after the test.
ex3_translation: We have a Chinese exam tomorrow.

notes: A common adjective for wanting something to drink.
ex1_translation: I'm very thirsty now and want to drink water.
ex2_translation: My younger brother is very thirsty after playing ball.
ex3_translation: After class I'm very thirsty and want some water.

notes: Use this for school classes or lessons.
ex1_translation: We have Chinese class in the afternoon.
ex2_translation: Today's lesson is very good.
ex3_translation: I like today's class.

notes: A school book used for class.
ex1_translation: My textbook is in my schoolbag.
ex2_translation: My older sister bought two textbooks.
ex3_translation: The teacher's textbook is on the table.

notes: A school text used for reading and study.
ex1_translation: The teacher tells us to read the text.
ex2_translation: My older sister is reading the lesson text at home.
ex3_sentence: 我们上午在学校读课文。
ex3_translation: We read the text at school this morning.

notes: Most often this means mouth. It can also mean an opening, and it is a common classifier for family members in some expressions.
ex1_translation: You have something in your mouth, so don't talk.
ex2_translation: He has water in his mouth, so he isn't talking.
ex3_translation: The child has food in his mouth.

notes: This often means a piece, and it is also a common money word for yuan.
ex1_translation: I want to eat a piece of bread.
ex2_translation: This schoolbag costs five yuan.
ex3_translation: This bread costs three yuan.

notes: Use it for speed, quick action, or something happening soon.
ex1_translation: Dad is driving very fast today.
ex2_translation: I'm almost home.
ex3_translation: You walk too fast.

notes: The basic verb for coming toward the speaker.
ex1_translation: Mom is here, let's eat.
ex2_translation: Are you coming to my home tomorrow?
ex3_translation: Why aren't you here yet?

notes: Use it for coming to or arriving at a place.
ex1_translation: Dad came to Beijing yesterday.
ex2_translation: I arrived at school very early today.
ex3_sentence: 今天我们上午来到机场。
ex3_translation: We arrived at the airport this morning.

notes: An adjective for age or something worn with age.
ex1_translation: My grandpa is really old now.
ex2_translation: Dad's car is very old.
ex3_translation: This house is very old.

notes: A respectful noun for an older person.
ex1_translation: That old person walks very slowly.
ex2_translation: I saw an elderly person on the road.
ex3_translation: That old person went home.

notes: The common word for a teacher.
ex1_sentence: 老师今天在教学楼上课。
ex1_translation: The teacher is teaching in the school building today.
ex2_translation: I like our teacher very much.
ex3_translation: The teacher came to school very early today.

notes: A grammar particle used for completed actions or a new state.
ex1_translation: I bought two books yesterday.
ex2_translation: It's gotten cold, and Mom has come home.
ex3_translation: I'm home now, what about you?

notes: An adjective for feeling tired.
ex1_translation: I'm very tired today and want to sleep.
ex2_translation: Mom is very tired after work.
ex3_translation: I'm too tired today and want to sleep.

notes: An adjective for cold weather or feeling cold.
ex1_sentence: 今天很冷，你多穿一点儿。
ex1_translation: It's very cold today, so wear a bit more clothing.
ex2_translation: It's cold outside, so don't go out.
ex3_translation: This cup of water is cold.

notes: A basic location word meaning inside or in. It is often used after a place word.
ex1_translation: There are two books in the schoolbag.
ex2_translation: I'm reading in the room.
ex3_translation: Mom is waiting for me in the car.

notes: A place word meaning inside.
ex1_translation: There is someone inside, please wait a moment.
ex2_translation: Mom is reading in the room.
ex3_translation: Inside this room is very clean.

notes: The common form of two before measure words.
ex1_translation: I have two cups.
ex2_translation: Mom bought two buns.
ex3_translation: I bought two buns.

notes: The number zero.
ex1_translation: It's 9:05 now.
ex2_translation: This is zero, not six.
ex3_translation: It is 10:01 now.

notes: The number six.
ex1_translation: My home is on the sixth floor.
ex2_translation: Today is June sixth.
ex3_translation: There are six people in my family.

notes: Use it for building floors.
ex1_translation: I have class on the sixth floor.
ex2_translation: My home is on the second floor.
ex3_translation: The shop is on the first floor.

notes: A location word meaning upstairs.
ex1_translation: My older sister is reading upstairs.
ex2_translation: Someone is having a meeting upstairs.
ex3_translation: Mom is cooking upstairs.

notes: A location word meaning downstairs.
ex1_translation: Mom is waiting for you downstairs.
ex2_translation: There is a restaurant downstairs.
ex3_translation: Mom is waiting for me downstairs.

notes: A common noun for a road or way.
ex1_translation: This road is not easy to walk on.
ex2_translation: The way to school is far.
ex3_translation: The road here is not easy to walk on.

notes: A noun for a road intersection.
ex1_translation: Let's meet at the intersection.
ex2_translation: That intersection is on the east side of the school.
ex3_translation: I am waiting for you at the intersection.

ex3_sentence: 北京真远，我们坐飞机吧。
ex3_translation: Beijing is really far, so let's go by plane.

notes: Commonly used as really in beginner examples.
ex1_translation: This book is really good.
ex2_translation: I really want to go to Beijing.
ex3_translation: The weather is really nice today.

notes: Most often this means exactly or right at this moment, depending on the sentence.
ex1_translation: I was just about to call you.
ex2_translation: He's just watching TV right now.
ex3_translation: I'm looking for my phone right now.

notes: A common progressive marker for actions happening now.
ex1_translation: Mom is currently making dinner at home.
ex2_translation: I'm in the middle of reading in the library.
ex3_sentence: 老师正在教学楼里上课。
ex3_translation: The teacher is currently teaching in the school building.

notes: The common verb meaning to know.
ex1_translation: I know this place now.
ex2_translation: My older sister doesn't know what time it is now.
ex3_translation: I know the station is over there.

notes: A noun meaning knowledge.
ex1_translation: This knowledge is very important to me.
ex2_translation: I've learned a lot about Chinese.
ex3_translation: There is a lot of knowledge in the textbook.

notes: Use this in patterns like 三个人中 for among and 名字中 for in. The middle sense is more common in fixed expressions and compounds.
ex1_translation: He is the tallest among the three of us.
ex2_translation: I am the youngest among the three children.
ex3_translation: This character is in the name.

notes: Use the country name China.
ex1_translation: I want to go to China.
ex2_translation: China is very big.
ex3_translation: My dad works in China.

notes: Use middle and in the middle for location.
ex1_translation: The book is in the middle of the table.
ex2_translation: I sit between Mom and Dad.
ex3_sentence: 学校在商店和医院中间。
ex3_translation: The school is between the shop and the hospital.

notes: Use Chinese as the language name.
ex1_translation: I can speak Chinese.
ex2_translation: I am learning Chinese.
ex3_translation: The teacher can speak Chinese.

notes: Use noon as the time word.
ex1_translation: We eat rice at noon.
ex2_translation: Mom goes home at noon.
ex3_translation: I eat at school at noon.

notes: Use the noun middle school.
ex1_translation: My older sister studies at a middle school.
ex2_translation: This middle school is very big.
ex3_translation: My home is behind the middle school.

notes: Use the noun middle school student.
ex1_translation: My older sister is a middle school student.
ex2_translation: That middle school student can speak Chinese.
ex3_sentence: 中学生中午在学校吃饭。
ex3_translation: Middle school students eat lunch at school at noon.

notes: Use heavy as the adjective.
ex1_translation: This schoolbag is heavy.
ex2_translation: This book is heavy.
ex3_translation: My bag is not heavy.

notes: Use important as the adjective.
ex1_translation: This is very important.
ex2_translation: Time is important.
ex3_translation: Studying Chinese is important.

notes: Most often this means live in a place. It can also mean to stay somewhere.
ex1_translation: I live in Beijing.
ex2_translation: Mom and Dad live in China.
ex3_translation: My family lives behind the school.

notes: Use prepare as the main gloss and get ready as a natural secondary gloss.
ex1_translation: I am preparing dinner.
ex2_translation: Mom is getting ready to go to the hospital.
ex3_translation: The teacher is preparing for class.

notes: Use the noun table.
ex1_translation: The book is on the table.
ex2_translation: There is a ball under the table.
ex3_translation: This table is big.

notes: Use character as the main gloss; word is a weaker but still useful secondary gloss.
ex1_translation: How do you write this character?
ex2_translation: I can write many Chinese characters.
ex3_translation: I do not know this character.

notes: Use 子 as the common noun suffix seen in words like 杯子, 桌子, and 包子.
ex1_translation: This cup is big.
ex2_translation: The teacher's table is very big.
ex3_translation: Mom bought buns.

notes: Use walk as the primary gloss and go where it sounds more natural.
ex1_translation: Let's go.
ex2_translation: You go first; I will come in a moment.
ex3_translation: I walk home.

notes: Use walk as the verb.
ex1_translation: I walk to school.
ex2_translation: Dad likes walking.
ex3_sentence: 晚上我们一起走路回家。
ex3_translation: We walk home together in the evening.

notes: Use most as the adverb.
ex1_translation: I like Chinese the most.
ex2_translation: I got to school the earliest today.
ex3_translation: I want to go to Beijing the most.

notes: Use best as the adjective or adverb.
ex1_translation: This one is the best.
ex2_translation: I think this time is the best.
ex3_translation: It is best to go by train.

notes: Use last as the primary gloss and final as a useful secondary gloss.
ex1_translation: I am the last to go home.
ex2_translation: The last character is the character for big.
ex3_translation: We go to the shop last.

notes: Use yesterday as the time word.
ex1_translation: I read at home yesterday.
ex2_translation: Mom went to the hospital yesterday.
ex3_sentence: 昨天晚上我们吃了包子。
ex3_translation: We ate buns last night.

notes: Use the direction left.
ex1_translation: Left is west, and right is east.
ex2_translation: I am on the left, and you are on the right.
ex3_translation: On a map, left is west.

notes: Left side is the clearest learner-facing gloss.
ex1_translation: There is a bookstore on the left side of the school.
ex2_translation: My bag is to your left.
ex3_translation: The cup on the left is mine.

notes: Use sit as the verb.
ex1_translation: Please sit.
ex2_translation: I sit behind you.
ex3_translation: Mom sits here and reads.

notes: Use the verb sit down.
ex1_translation: Please sit down.
ex2_translation: Everyone, sit down.
ex3_translation: Sit down and read first.

notes: Use do as the main gloss and make when it is the clearer English choice in context.
ex1_translation: Mom is cooking at home.
ex2_translation: This bun was made by Mom.
ex3_translation: What are you doing?
